message.content: In Christian tradition, the figure most central to the faith is Jesus Christ, who is regarded as the Son of God and the fulfillment of the prophetic tradition. However, Christianity also honors many other prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and John the Baptist—who played crucial roles in shaping the narrative and theology of the faith. Different Christian communities may emphasize different aspects of prophetic history, but Jesus is generally considered the pivotal figure around whom Christian belief revolves.
